Workflow Editor

6. Workflow Editor

The Workflow editor builds an ordered sequence of steps. The current step types are:

  • Assert — check a condition and fail the workflow if it is not true.
  • Set Variable — create or update a workflow variable.
  • Output — publish a value as a final workflow result column. It does not control a Powers output.
  • Wait — wait for a specified duration.
  • Tool Action — invoke an action on a configured Tool Instance, such as a Powers set or output action or a Meters measurement.
  • For — repeat a body over an exact decimal range.
  • While — repeat a body while a condition remains true.
  • If / Else — run either THEN or ELSE once based on a comparison; ELSE may be empty.

The Steps categories keep this fixed relative order: Workflow, Background Workflow, FG/BG Interaction, Meters, Powers, Scopes, Serial. Available categories appear first. Locked categories are moved to Unavailable categories (N) at the bottom of the list. This group starts collapsed; expand it to see each locked category and its existing reason. When no categories are locked, the group is hidden. Workflow is always available. Background Workflow requires a Background binding in Setup; FG/BG Interaction also requires Enable FG/BG Interaction in the Workflow sidebar. Instrument categories require a matching Tool Instance in the Template. Locked categories cannot expand or be selected. Adding or removing bindings or instances updates the grouping without deleting existing Steps. Live Resources, executable configuration, capabilities, and Execution Mode do not affect these locks.

Click an available category header to expand or collapse it independently. Expanded categories show −; collapsed categories show + and hide their step buttons. Available categories start expanded when the app opens; changing availability does not erase their individual expand/collapse choices. A successful New or Open Template resets the unavailable group to collapsed. UI expansion states are not saved in Templates. Scopes File Output remains a separate panel with its own expand/collapse state and the same Scopes Instance lock.

Steps can be placed in the root workflow, loop bodies, or If branches. Use the step properties area to edit the selected step. Use Validate when you want to check the current Template before running; Simulation and Live also validate the Template when the run starts, so pressing Validate first is useful but is not a separate run prerequisite. Use the pencil beside Step ID in Properties to rename a step. Press Enter or Save to apply; Escape or Cancel discards the edit. IDs must use lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens between segments and be unique throughout the Workflow. Renaming also updates references to that step. Editing is unavailable while the Workflow is busy.

In Steps, hover over any available step type to see its short native tooltip describing the action. Click a step type to select it; clicking does not insert it. Selected Step and Add Step stay above the scrollable categories. Add Step is disabled until a type is selected. Press it to insert into the location shown by ADDING STEP TO. After insertion the palette selection clears, while the inserted Workflow step remains selected for editing. Set Target to Root switches the destination without inserting a step. Creating or opening a Template also clears the palette selection. All Step Palette buttons use a consistent single-line height. Long labels are shortened or truncated; their native tooltip preserves the full name and action description.

Alternatively, drag a Step type from Steps into Sequence to insert it at the drop position, independently of the ADDING STEP TO target. Drop before or after a Step, at the end of Root, or into an empty or populated IF THEN / ELSE, FOR, or WHILE body. Dropping outside a valid destination does not add a Step. After a successful drop, the new Step is selected in Properties and the Palette selection clears. Drag-to-add is unavailable while editing is busy.

Validate, Run Simulation / Run Live, Stop Workflow, and active loop Stop controls appear at the top-right of the Workflow summary, beside Template and Steps. Validation, running, Stop, and run failure feedback appears below these controls, above the Builder. Detailed run errors remain available there. Controls wrap when the window is narrow. Clear Workflow stays in the Sequence header.

The Step Display Density menu to the right of Clear Workflow offers Compact, Standard (default), and Comfortable. The density preference is stored locally and applies across Templates; it does not change Workflow data.

In Sequence, each FOR, WHILE, and IF step has its own expand/collapse arrow. IF also lets you collapse THEN and ELSE independently. Expand All and Collapse All appear below the Sequence heading. Collapsing hides nested steps but keeps their count and any selection, validation, or run failure indication visible. Switching tabs keeps the current view; creating or opening a Template expands all steps. Expand a body before dragging into it; Add Step reveals a collapsed destination after successful insertion.

Editing Workflow steps, execution settings in Tool Setup, or Background bindings and setup immediately hides the previous run failure or Live startup error from the Workflow summary. Pressing Validate also hides that feedback immediately, even without edits. Validation shows its own result; Valid does not guarantee that a run will succeed. A new failed run shows its own error and Technical details. Selecting steps, switching tabs, and changing display options keep the current error feedback.

These actions preserve Last Run's original status, diagnostics, Execution Results, committed Output rows, Background datasets, and partial export. A failed Last Run remains failed in Output. Live Preflight failures keep their separate feedback and mean that the Live run has not started.

In Sequence, click a step to select it. Ctrl+Click adds or removes an individual step; Shift+Click selects the range from the selection anchor. Multi-selection stays within one sibling list: root steps or the body of one For or While. Ctrl/Shift-clicking another list starts a new selection there. Properties can edit only one step; multiple selected steps show their count.

Drag the handle beside a step to reorder it or move it between Root, For bodies, and While bodies. Drop on a card's upper or lower half to insert before or after it; drop in a body's blank area to append, including empty bodies. The insertion line shows the destination. Use the blank area at the end of the Root list to move steps back to Root. Dragging a selected step moves the whole selection, including non-adjacent steps, in their original relative order. Moving a loop keeps its whole body. IDs, parameters, bindings and references are preserved. The editor prevents moving a loop into itself or a descendant and prevents loop depth beyond five. It does not validate execution semantics during dragging. The Sequence scrolls when dragging near its top or bottom edge.

Up / Down move the selection one position within its list; the operation is disabled when any selected step reaches that boundary. The Delete button on a selected step deletes the selection; on an unselected step it deletes only that step. Deleting a loop also deletes its body.

With focus in the Workflow editor:

  • Ctrl+C copies the selected steps.
  • Ctrl+X cuts the selected steps to the application's internal clipboard. The first paste preserves original IDs and internal references when IDs do not conflict. Later pastes, or a conflicting first paste, use Copy/Paste ID remapping and unique Output names. Output name or Page conflicts follow existing Paste rules.
  • Ctrl+V pastes after the last selected step, or at the Root end when none is selected. The pasted steps become the new selection.
  • Delete deletes the current selection; without a selection it does nothing.
  • Ctrl+A selects the direct siblings of the active step, or Root steps if nothing is selected. It does not also select steps inside nested loop bodies.

The internal clipboard lasts for this application session. Inputs, text areas, selects and editable text keep their native shortcuts. While the Workflow is busy, selection and Copy remain available, but dragging, Up/Down, Cut, Delete and Paste are disabled.

Validate, Run Simulation, and Run Live use the same Core Template validation. On failure, the overall error remains visible. When the error reliably identifies a step, its card has a red border and warning icon; select it to see the reason in Properties. Errors without a reliable step location remain overall errors. Editing the Workflow clears old validation marks; only the next Validate or Run checks again. Invalid Templates do not start workers. Use Validate after moving steps to check references and scopes: a For variable cannot be used outside its body unless a value already exists in that enclosing scope. Ordinary variables created inside a loop are local to each iteration; updates to inherited variables persist. Validation checks statically unavailable variables, while value-dependent errors remain runtime checks.
